guide.summary: Production CCB, church-wide: id resolution, sensitive data, paging, rate limits, hatches.
guide.content:
# Church Community Builder usage

Production church data, church-wide under one administrator-approved grant (System Auth), reads plus approval-gated writes: Pastoral care and group shepherding

The OAuth client is configured for this environment; use the connection's existing grant. Resolve a person's identity with get_me when needed.

Sensitive fields: drop. Named projections stay narrow; credentials and private file destinations are always withheld.

Configured scopes: read:advanced_searches read:campuses read:church read:event_attendance read:events read:forms read:group_members read:groups read:individual_groups read:individual_notes read:individual_pledges read:individuals read:individuals_metrics read:process_queues read:queue_individuals read:scheduling write:event_attendance write:events write:form_responses write:group_members write:groups write:individual_groups write:individual_notes write:individuals write:notes write:queue_individuals write:scheduling.

## People, households and groups

CCB v2 addresses records by integer ids. Resolve a person from the individual
list and a household from families; never guess ids. Family membership and
church group membership join by individual id. A membership role belongs to
that group, rather than being a property of the person everywhere.

Identity Auth acts with the signed-in person's permissions. A permission
refusal can mean that person lacks access even when the connection is healthy.

## Events and attendance

An event is a series; its dated occurrence is a separate identity. Attendance
joins need both the event id and occurrence. Preserve the vendor's date and
time-zone meaning instead of treating every occurrence as UTC midnight.

## Pastoral and financial records

Notes, background checks, pledges and giving metrics can be sensitive. Read
only what the task needs and reduce those records inside execute_code before
returning an answer. Gift metrics are counts by period, with a range of at
most twelve months. Per-gift transactions and amounts belong to the legacy
v1 XML API, which this v2 connector does not reach.

## Vendor call rates and recovery

CCB meters endpoints separately per API client. Individual profile reads have
no burst; individual advanced searches allow one call per five seconds, and
category schedule lists allow one per two seconds. Prefer list pages over a
loop of individual gets. Other deployments sharing the client spend from the
same vendor allowance.

For a profile edit, resolve the individual first and preserve fields outside
the requested change. After an ambiguous update, read that profile to determine
what actually changed before deciding whether another write is needed.

## Conventions

- **Paging:** a paged `list_*` or `search_*` read takes `limit` (default 25, at most 100) and `cursor`. While `page.hasMore` is true, pass `page.nextCursor` back unchanged as `cursor`; the last page has no `nextCursor`.
- **Paging:** on a paged hatch read, keep the original method, path, filters, limit and fields. Pass `page.nextCursor` unchanged as the top-level `cursor`; omit raw anchors on continuations. The last page has `page.hasMore: false` and no `nextCursor`. If `page.hasMore` is true without a cursor, the data is incomplete and continuation could not be confined.
- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `ccb_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `ccb_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `ccb_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `ccb_api_write` calls a reviewed write, and every call to it needs approval. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused; these are refused by design: `POST /church/privacy_defaults`, `POST /data_import/individuals`, `POST /data_import/sacraments`, `POST /events/{id}/photo`, `POST /families/{id}/photo`, `POST /files`, `POST /forms/{id}/responses`, `POST /groups/{id}/photo`, `POST /individuals/{id}/files/{file_id}`, `POST /individuals/{id}/files`, `POST /individuals/{id}/photo`, `POST /messages/{id}/comments`, `POST /oauth/token`, `POST /reset_password`, `POST /scheduling/categories/{id}/files`, `POST /scheduling/categories/{id}/messages`, `POST /scheduling/categories/{id}/notifications`, `POST /scheduling/events/{id}/files`, `PUT /individuals/{id}/assignments`, `PUT /individuals/{id}/groups/{group_id}`, `PUT /individuals/{id}/privacy_settings`, `PUT /messages/{id}/comments/{comment_id}`, `PUT /messages/{id}`, `PUT /scheduling/families/{id}/assignments`.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. `not_found` means the record does not exist; this API tells absence from a permission gap. It documents no conflict.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the CCB individual the access token belongs to. Under Identity Auth that is the signed-in person whose permissions every call carries.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_individuals
tools.description: Find CCB individuals by partial name, phone, or email. Returns lean profiles with family and campus ids; not the advanced search.

query.description: Partial name, phone number, or email. Omit to page everyone.

campusScope.description: Campuses to search relative to the connection's own.

limit.description: Allowed page sizes are 25, 50, 75, and 100. The vendor default is 25.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: get_individual
tools.description: Get one CCB individual's profile: contact, addresses, membership, and custom fields. CCB allows one call a second; prefer list_individuals for many people.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.description: Search CCB church records with a reviewed read-only POST. Returns common identifiers, name, status and contact summaries; use the indexed read hatch for domain-specific response fields.

domain.description: Reviewed advanced-search domain; the pattern lists every allowed value.

body.description: Vendor search configuration and filters; get the operation details before choosing them.

limit.description: Allowed page sizes are 25, 50, 75, and 100. The vendor default is 25.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: ccb_api_search
tools.description: Find CCB API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; ccb_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: ccb_api_details
tools.description: Read one CCB API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: ccb_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed CCB API read, including reviewed read-only POST. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. Read people and individual profiles, households and families, groups and memberships, events and attendance, campuses, forms and responses, processes and queues, schedules and assignments, notes, pledges and giving metrics. Discover the exact operation with ccb_api_search, then inspect ccb_api_details.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /individuals/42. No query string.

method.description: GET by default; another method only for an operation search routes here.

body.description: Body for a reviewed read-only POST.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from this same read; omit raw query anchors when continuing.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

param.description: Vendor parameter restored from cursor; pass nextCursor as the top-level cursor.

tools.name: ccb_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed CCB API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. Update, edit or change a person's email or phone; create people and individual profiles, pastoral notes, group memberships and events. Discover the exact operation with ccb_api_search, then inspect ccb_api_details. Writes require authorized configured scopes.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /individuals/42. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
